current_behaviour: AAFC blue (#51b0e3) used in some text contexts. On light backgrounds (#f4f8fc or #ffffff), the contrast ratio is approximately 2.26:1 (white) to 2.41:1 (page background). WCAG 2.2 requires 4.5:1 for normal text, 3:1 for large/bold text.
expected_behaviour: Blue as text colour must be used only on dark backgrounds (≥3:1 contrast) or replaced with --dark (#002f65, 21:1 on white) for body text usage.
reproduction: CSS audit: grep 'color:var(--blue)' and 'color:#51b0e3' in index.html; for each result determine the background context and compute contrast ratio.
evidence: index.html lines 234, 244 (.tb-wm .r — on dark header, PASSES). index.html line 234 (.auth-back-btn — on dark auth bg, PASSES). May be additional usages in inline styles or JS-rendered content.
root_cause: Design token choice made before WCAG audit. Blue accent serves as interactive affordance at low contrast.
dependencies: Requires full CSS audit to enumerate all text usages of var(--blue)
risk: WCAG AA failure. Accessibility non-compliance on light-surface blue text. Could affect users with low vision.
implementation_plan: Run CSS audit for all color:var(--blue) and color:#51b0e3 usages. For each: if on light bg, replace with var(--royal) (#004b8d, 7.3:1 on white) or var(--dark) (#002f65). Do not change border, background, or shadow usages.
test_plan: After fix: automated contrast check via axe-core or manual computation. Assert each fixed element has contrast ≥ 4.5:1 (normal text) or ≥ 3:1 (large/bold).
remaining_work: Full CSS audit for blue-as-text on light backgrounds. Replace with --royal or --dark where failing.
